title: Epic t8u's A1 measures the -short gate, which skips this epic's own subjects
body:
Epic t8u's first acceptance criterion is written against 'the full gate', and the epic's description measures the gate at 'roughly 20 minutes'. That was true when the epic was created (2026-09-18). Two days later tick miu made -short mean something (internal/shorttest, 2026-09-20): the per-tick gate is now `go test -short …`, internal/reconcile, internal/exec/herdr and internal/runstate skip their end-to-end tests under it, and .tick/runners.toml records the gate running in seconds-to-minutes. Every wall-clock cost this epic profiles — internal/reconcile's 1148-git-process end-to-end tests, the runstate spinners tick 1qy just removed — lives in the FULL suite, which is what CI's go job and epic close-out run. A close-out that times the declared -short command before and after will measure a suite this epic barely touches and produce a meaningless verdict either way: 'already under half' by miu's work, or an unreachable target. The fix is to re-word the criterion to name the full suite; the exact tracker edit is attached and the run's writer can apply it.
evidence: .tick/runners.toml:155-163 ('the `-short` in this line now MEANS something (tick miu) … this command runs in seconds'); internal/shorttest/shorttest.go:22-30; make gate = go test -short (Makefile:77); both concurrent-fetch tests SKIP under -short, verified
tracker edit: acceptance_criteria of t8u (applied by the run)
